key_insight: A single end-to-end model can generate a patient-specific cardiac surface mesh directly from 3D CT or MRI, skipping the usual segmentation-to-mesh post-processing pipeline.
clinical_relevance: This could make cardiac digital twin workflows faster, more consistent, and easier to use in settings that need simulation-ready heart models.
method: 3D Swin Transformer encoder-decoder extracts volumetric features from CT/MRI.
Graph Attention Network deforms a template mesh to match the cardiac boundary.
One forward pass produces a smooth, simulation-ready surface mesh without Marching Cubes or manual cleanup.
evidence_signal: On MM-WHS 2017, the model reported Dice scores of 0.84 for CT and 0.83 for MRI, with mean Chamfer distance of 1.8 mm and 95th-percentile surface distance below 5 mm.
watch_item: The approach still needs validation beyond a benchmark dataset, especially for anatomical edge cases and real-world clinical deployment robustness.
paper_title: Transformer-Guided Graph Attention for Direct Cardiac Mesh Reconstruction: A Structural Digital Twin Framework
